questions.solution:
$(2 x)^{2 y}=4 \mathrme^{2 x-2 y}$
Taking log on both sides, we get
$\begin{aligned}
& 2 y \log 2 x=\log \left(4 \mathrme^{2 x-2 y}\right) \\
& \Rightarrow 2 y \log 2 x=\log 4+\log \mathrme^{2 x-2 y} \\
& \Rightarrow 2 y \log 2 x=\log 4+2 x-2 y \\
& \Rightarrow 2 y \log 2 x+2 y=\log 4+2 x \\
& \Rightarrow 2(y \log 2 x+y)=2 \log 2+2 x \\
& \Rightarrow y \log 2 x+y=\log 2+x \\
& \Rightarrow y(1+\log 2 x)=x+\log 2 \\
& \Rightarrow y=\frac{x+\log 2}{1+\log 2 x}
\end{aligned}$
Differentiating w.r.t. $x$, we get
$\begin{gathered}
\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=\frac{(1+\log 2 x)(1+0)-(x+\log 2)\left(\frac{1}{2 x}\right) \cdot 2}{(1+\log 2 x)^2} \\
\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=\frac{(1+\log 2 x)-\frac{1}{x}(x+\log 2)}{(1+\log 2 x)^2} \\
\Rightarrow(1+\log 2 x)^2 \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=1+\log 2 x-1-\frac{\log 2}{x} \\
\Rightarrow(1+\log 2 x)^2 \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{ d} x}=\log 2 x-\frac{\log 2}{x} \\
=\frac{x \log 2 x-\log 2}{x}
\end{gathered}$

questions.q: The equation of normal to the curve $y=(1+x)^{y}+\sin ^{-1}  \left(\sin ^{2}x\right)$ at $x=0 is$
questions.solution:
Given the curve $y = (1+x)^{y} + \sin^{-1}(\sin^{2}x)$.

At $x = 0$, $y = (1+0)^{y} + \sin^{-1}(\sin^{2}0) = 1^{y} + 0 = 1$. Thus, the point of contact is $(0, 1)$.

To find the slope of the tangent, differentiate the equation with respect to $x$:
Let $u = (1+x)^{y}$. Then $\ln u = y \ln(1+x)$.
Differentiating with respect to $x$: $\dfrac{1}{u} \dfrac{du}{dx} = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \ln(1+x) + \dfrac{y}{1+x}$.
So, $\dfrac{du}{dx} = (1+x)^{y} \left[ \dfrac{dy}{dx} \ln($1+x) + $\dfrac{y}{1+x} \right].
At $(0, 1)$, \dfrac{du}{dx} =$1^{1} [ $\dfrac{dy}{dx} \ln($1) + $\dfrac{1}{1} ] =$1$.

Now differentiate $\sin^{-1}(\sin^{2}x)$ with respect to $x$:
\dfrac{d}{dx} [\sin^{-1}(\sin^{2}$x)] = $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - (\sin^{2}x)^{2}}} \cdot$2 \sin x \cos x = $\dfrac{\sin 2x}{\sqrt{1 - \sin^{4}x}}.
At $x = 0$, this derivative is \dfrac{0}{1} =$0$.

Therefore, \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{du}{dx} +$0 = 1 + 0 = 1$.
The slope of the tangent $m = 1$.

The slope of the normal $m_{\perp} = -$\dfrac{1}{m} = -$1$.
The equation of the normal at $(0, 1)$ is $y - 1 = -1(x - 0)$.
$y - 1 = -x \Rightarrow x + y = 1$.

Answer: $x+y=1
